statement.p: Find the area between y = 6 \sin x and y = 7 \cos x over the interval \left[0,\pi\right]. Sketch the curves if necessary.

static.solution:
Over the interval [0,\pi], the graphs y = 6\sin x and y = 7 \cos x intersect when 6\sin x = 7 \cos x, i.e., \tan x = \frac{7}{6}, i.e., x=\tan^{-1}(\frac{7}{6})=0.862170054667226.
Let t = \tan^{-1}(\frac{7}{6}).
Over the interval \left[0, t\right], the graph of y = 6\sin x lies below that of y = 7 \cos x. Hence, the area between the two curves is \int_0^{ t}(7 \cos x-6 \sin x)dx \begin{array}{ll} \amp =\left.(7\sin x+6\cos x)\right|_0^{ t} \cr \amp =\left(7\sin t+6\cos t\right)-(7\cdot 0+6\cdot 1)\cr \amp =\left(7\sin t+6\cos t\right)-6 \end{array}
Since t = \tan^{-1}(\frac{7}{6}), we have \tan t = \frac{7}{6}. Considering a rightangle triangle with an angle which opposite side has length 7 and adjacent side has length 6, we see that the hypotenues is \sqrt{85}. Thus \sin t = \frac{7}{\sqrt{85}} and \cos t = \frac{6}{\sqrt{85}}.
7\sin t+6\cos t = \frac{7^2}{\sqrt{85}} + \frac{6^2}{\sqrt{85}} = \frac{7^2+6^2}{\sqrt{85}} = \frac{85}{\sqrt{85}}=\sqrt{85}.
Thus, \int_0^{ t}(7 \cos x-6 \sin x)dx= \sqrt{85}-6.
Over the interval \left[ t,\pi\right], the graph of y = 6\sin x lies above that of y = 7 \cos x. Hence, the area between the two curves is \int^\pi_{ t}(6\sin x - 7 \cos x)dx \begin{array}{ll} \amp =-\left.(7\sin x+6\cos x)\right|^\pi_{ t} \cr \amp =6 + \sqrt{85} \end{array}
Thus the total area is the sum of the above two integrals, which is 2\sqrt{85}.
